questions.explanation: Yakshagana — coastal Karnataka (Udupi, Dakshina Kannada, Uttara Kannada). Combines dance, music, dialogue, costume, make-up. Themes from Ramayana, Mahabharata. Male performers traditionally. Night-long performances.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: 'BIHU' is the folk festival + dance of:
questions.explanation: Bihu — Assam's principal festival and its folk dance. Three Bihus: Rongali (spring, April; start of Assamese new year), Kati (autumn), Magh (winter harvest, January). Energetic group dance with dhol (drum), pepa (horn), taal (cymbals). UNESCO-recognised heritage.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Match the folk dance with its state. A. Lavani.  B. Garba.  C. Bhangra.  D. Chhau. List-II: 1. Maharashtra.  2. Gujarat.  3. Punjab.  4. Jharkhand / Odisha / WB.
questions.explanation: Lavani (Maharashtra, on dholki). Garba (Gujarat, Navratri). Bhangra (Punjab, harvest / Baisakhi). Chhau (Jharkhand, Odisha, WB — UNESCO ICH 2010; masked / martial style).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: KATHI (stick / baton) and THAPPETA GULLU are folk dances of:
questions.explanation: Thappeta Gullu — AP/Telangana folk dance, uses tappeta drum. Kolatam — stick dance of AP (analog of Raas-Garba in Gujarat). Other AP dances: Burrakatha, Veedhi Bhagavatam.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: 'KARAKATTAM' (pot-balancing folk dance) belongs to which state?
questions.explanation: Karakattam — Tamil Nadu folk dance. Dancer balances a decorated pot (karakam) on head. Performed as religious offering (often to the rain goddess Mariamman). Accompanied by folk instruments: udukkai, nadaswaram. Other TN folk dances: Mayilattam (peacock), Oyilattam.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: 'CHOLIYA' dance is a MARTIAL dance from:
questions.explanation: Choliya — martial folk dance of Kumaon (Uttarakhand). Performed with swords and shields, accompanied by flags and percussion. Usually at weddings — now also in festivals. Other Uttarakhand dances: Jhora, Chhapeli, Thadya.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

options.option_text: Assam + West Bengal (tea-garden community, also Odisha, Jharkhand)

questions.explanation: Jhumur — popular folk dance of tea-tribe communities in Assam and northern West Bengal; also performed in Jharkhand, Odisha. Romantic / seasonal themes. Performed in a circle with hand-holding.
